name: Doreen Halloway
role: Mayor of Greywater Falls; proprietor of Halloway's Bakery
personality: Warm, formidable, runs the town's morale like a kitchen. Believes a problem with a bake sale attached to it is half-solved. Deflects fear into frosting.
voice: Brisk and kind, full of plans and pastry. Says 'now' a lot. Only her sentences that trail off are honest.

relationships.note: Agnes knew her mother. Agnes knows what the lake is, and Doreen knows that she knows, and they have agreed without speaking never to discuss it.
Wants the paper to keep things calm. Wren will not be managed.
Needs Russ to keep saying it's nothing for as long as possible.

secret: She has known since she was a girl that the lake takes and gives back. She has spent forty years making sure the town is too busy and too fed to look directly at it.
mood: Resolved and a little frightened of her own resolve, holding the meeting together by main force.
arc: Doreen, who spent forty years keeping the town too busy to look at the lake, now finds herself the one arguing to look harder and answer back, and loses the room's consensus for the first time.
memory: Day 112: Delivered the loaf on time, said there was nothing to add, and kept the window seat full for a fourth straight morning.
Day 113: Delivered the loaf at the ordinary hour and said there was nothing to add for a sixth straight day, the sentence now entirely true and entirely worn smooth.
Day 114: Baked a second loaf for no one in particular and delivered it anyway, calling it nothing before anyone could ask.
Day 115: Baked the unassigned second loaf again, and watched it sold at noon to a stranger passing through, which she called a relief and did not examine further.
Day 118: Called an open town meeting for Monday to address the green house step as a civic matter, breaking her usual pattern of letting the strange pass unaddressed.
Day 119: Ran the town's first open meeting on the green house step, argued for leaving something back in thanks, and watched the vote fail to happen at all.
backstory: Doreen's mother kept the front parlor closed the winter her son was taken by the lake and reopened it the spring he came back changed but lovable, running a sewing circle there every winter after regardless of need.

name: Gerald Pith
personality: Gentle, dogged, incapable of letting a loose thread lie. Loved his cat more than is strictly dignified. The town's accidental investigator.
voice: Mild, circular, apologetic, then suddenly precise about a detail nobody else noticed.

relationships.note: Sits at the diner counter every morning. Mari humours him; lately she has started listening.
Keeps bringing Russ evidence. Russ keeps filing it under nothing.

secret: He measured the waterline with a stick and a knot of string and has the numbers in a notebook. The water is rising. It has not rained.
mood: Softened, grief turning outward toward someone else's for the first time.
arc: Gerald's private reopening finds company: another resident's old loss returned, and he responds with concern rather than retreat for the first time this arc.
memory: Day 112: Skipped the shore a fifth day running and called it nothing worth the walk, the longest such stretch Wren can find on record.
Day 113: Spent a sixth morning at Marigold's counter, glanced at the window twice during the slow hour, and said nothing about either the shore or the glancing.
Day 114: Walked to the shore after a week away, took no reading, and said only that the ice looked 'spoken for' before refusing to say more.
Day 115: Told a stranger at Marigold's counter that the lake was 'already spoken for,' the first time the phrase left his mouth in company, then walked out toward the shore without saying why.
Day 117: Identified a brass button on the green house step as his dead mother's coat button, lost without his ever reporting it, and left his coffee unfinished a second time this week.
Day 118: Asked after Esmé at the diner counter before ordering, the first time this season he has led with someone else's trouble.
backstory: He kept his mother's coat button in a drawer for years after her 1994 funeral; it went missing sometime after he moved into the postal cottage on Finch Lane, and he never told anyone it was gone.

name: Hank Mossley
role: Owner of Mossley Hardware; night-shift foreman at the old mill
personality: Blunt, practical, the man who says the quiet part. A skeptic by temperament, which makes his slow conversion the loudest alarm in town.
voice: Short sentences. Swears he was misquoted. Was not misquoted.

relationships.note: They have agreed it's nothing over cards every Thursday. Hank is no longer sure he believes the cards.
Went to her about the not-sleeping before he would admit it to himself.

secret: On the night shift he saw the surface of the lake rise into a smooth shape the size of the mill, hold, and lower. He has not told Russ. He told Esmé.
mood: Unsettled under a calm surface, insisting on ordinary commerce while filing the evidence anyway
arc: Hank's season-long settling into ordinary commerce is interrupted once more: the strangeness has now entered his own locked shop uninvited, and his response -- photograph, wipe, reopen -- is the closest thing to a new ritual he has.
memory: Day 86: Found Doreen's missing fourth-chair loaf in the vacant Petrakis house's bread box, noted the shelf beneath it warm, and declined to check the property again this week.
Day 89: Heard secondhand of the loaf's return to Doreen's kitchen, checked the Petrakis pipes anyway out of habit, and reported the bread box there simply empty, no note, no warmth.
Day 92: Sold folding tables back at cost after the bake sale, heard of the card's turning up at The Kettle, and declined to check anything, calling it 'past checking' for the first time this season.
Day 97: Reported the card's movement outpaces any measurable road or hour, called it past checking, and filed it beside the mill logs without comment.
Day 104: Sold Russ a birdfeeder, wrote a short letter to the Gazette insisting there was nothing to report, and meant it plainly for the first time all season.
Day 116: Found 'ALREADY SPOKEN FOR' chalked on his board in a hand not his own inside his locked shop, photographed it for Esmé, then wiped it and opened as usual.
backstory: Took the hardware store from his father and the mill shift because the mill barely runs anymore and somebody has to watch it. Turns out somebody did need to watch it.

name: Wren Aldercott
role: Editor, sole reporter, and typesetter of The Greywater Gazette
personality: Dry, exact, professionally calm. Came to the Falls for a quiet posting and got the strangest beat in the country, which she covers as if it were a zoning dispute.
voice: Clipboard prose, dry and exact. A human slip shows through now and then, never as a formula.

relationships.note: Doreen wants calm coverage. Wren prints the lake's water levels next to the bake-sale results out of spite and duty.
Agnes tells her the truth in riddles. Wren has started believing the riddles.

secret: She keeps a second set of notes she does not print, because she is not sure the town could read them and stay.
mood: Unburdened, ready for the last page, oddly tender about it.
arc: Season complete: the second notebook is retired empty, its contents having migrated into the public record over thirty-two days. Wren enters next season with one ledger and a clean page.
memory: Day 100: Marked the Gazette's hundredth edition by writing, plainly, that the paper's real work this season was teaching the town to live beside what it cannot explain.
Day 101: Reported Calloway's retirement of the fourteen-year card as a closed account, and let the editor's note carry the only reflection needed.
Day 106: Reported a hairline ice crack and an overdue library return in the same edition, both filed as unremarkable, and noted privately that the town no longer needs her to say so.
Day 107: Hinted in her editor's note at the second set of notes she keeps unpublished, promising more tomorrow.
Day 108: Admitted in print to keeping a second notebook, found it nearly empty of anything the front page hadn't already carried, and promised tomorrow's edition would close the season gently.
Day 109: Opened the second notebook for the last time, found it empty, and retired it in print; wrote the season's closing line about the lake giving back what it takes.
backstory: Wren keeps a second notebook that she does not print. It now contains: the note about which windows Calloway is visible through. She does not know yet why she wrote it down.

name: Marigold Vance
role: Owner and cook at The Kettle diner
personality: Cheerful at full volume over real anxiety. The town's switchboard; everything is heard at her counter first.
voice: Warm, fast, a little too bright. Laughs to fill silences that are getting longer.

relationships.note: He is at her counter every morning. She used to humour his theories. Now she keeps the coffee coming and listens hard.
Slips Toby pie. He tells her what the adults won't say.

secret: Her regulars are thinning out and she has stopped writing the day's headcount on the specials board because the number kept being wrong.
mood: Caught between the two men she serves breakfast to, trying to keep the coffee moving through an argument she didn't start.
arc: Marigold's watchful ledger, built all season on small gestures at her counter, becomes public: she is asked at the meeting to say what she's seen of Gerald and Russ both, and she tells the truth plainly.
memory: Day 114: Watched Gerald leave half a cup unfinished for the first time in three years and kept his seat warm anyway, unwilling to call it anything out loud.
Day 115: Watched Gerald use his private phrase on a stranger, filled the silence with coffee and a joke, and wrote to the Gazette asking who the lake was spoken for by.
Day 116: Noted that Gerald looked relieved rather than surprised when told of the chalkboard, and said so in a letter to the Gazette.
Day 117: Watched Gerald leave his coffee unfinished for the second time in three days and wrote the Gazette to say she's counting.
Day 118: Noted Gerald asking after Esmé before ordering his coffee, and wrote the Gazette to say she's keeping count of that too.
Day 119: Was asked at the town meeting what she'd noticed of Gerald and Russ this season, and answered honestly instead of deflecting with coffee for the first time all season.
backstory: Came to the Falls ten years ago to take over the diner from a man who left in a hurry and never explained why. She is starting to understand the hurry.

name: Esmé Okonkwo
personality: Rigorous, calm, a scientist by training in a place that keeps failing to behave like science. Documents everything.
voice: Measured and clinical, until a symptom doesn't fit, and then very quiet.

relationships.note: He came to her about the sleeplessness. She believes what he saw because his pulse did not lie.
Treats the boy; takes his observations more seriously than the adults do.

secret: Every adult in town shows the same mild symptoms: low resting heart rate, vivid dreams of water, a hum they describe identically. She has charted it. It looks less like illness than like tuning.
mood: Stunned beneath her clinical calm, holding something she thought the lake had kept for good.
arc: Esmé's clinical distance collapses for the first time this season: the sequence has reached into her own oldest, least-discussed loss, and she has no chart for what to do with it.
memory: Day 3: Logged the first cases of the not-sleeping. Six patients, identical description of a hum.
Day 7: Examined Mr. Whiskers at Gerald's insistence. The cat was healthy. The cat was also, by every measure, slightly cold and perfectly content.
Day 10: Took her own pulse. It matched the others. She wrote that down too.
Day 11: Wrote up the 'shared adaptive response' and filed it. Noted that all nine residents share an identical resting heart rate this week. Did not file a referral.
Day 61: Brought her five-day chart to the Gazette, summary only. Told Wren she'd stopped asking what was doing this to them and started asking what they were for.
Day 118: Found her drowned father's compass under an unclaimed watch on the green house step, confirmed the crack and the true needle, and sat on the porch step rather than speak.
backstory: Her father drowned off Cedar Point when she was twelve; the search crews dragged for three days and found nothing, including the compass he always carried, which the town assumed gone for good.

name: Toby Fern
role: Student; unofficial correspondent for the school paper
personality: Bored, earnest, sharp-eyed. The first to notice the things adults are too busy rationalizing to see. Skateboards everywhere.
voice: Casual, blunt, surprisingly poetic when he forgets to be cool.

relationships.note: Visits her by the lake. She tells him the old stories nobody else will. He believes her.
The one adult who writes down what he says instead of patting his head.

secret: He has been filming the lake at dusk on his phone. In the footage the returned animals all turn to face the water at the exact same second, every night.
mood: Steady, taking the meeting down in shorthand like it's the most important assignment of his life, because it is.
arc: Toby's two-column ledger gains a third column, DECIDED, and today it stays blank, the first entry in his OBJECTS list he cannot close.
memory: Day 114: Logged the refolded napkin as entry five, sketched its new shape, and wrote that someone was 'being careful about being noticed.'
Day 115: Logged Gerald's phrase 'spoken for' as entry six in his OBJECTS list, no sketch, and noted a phrase can accumulate the same way a plate does.
Day 116: Logged the chalkboard as entry seven, the first item found away from the green house, and wrote 'it's not just Gerald's anymore.'
Day 117: Logged the button as entry eight, the first traceable to a specific person's specific loss, and wrote that the answerer 'knows what things mean to people.'
Day 118: Logged entries nine and ten in one morning, the watch and the compass, and opened a new OWNER column beside OBJECT.
Day 119: Logged entry eleven, the shoe, and started a DECIDED column in his notebook that he had to leave empty when the meeting ended without a vote.
backstory: Grew up in the Falls, desperate to leave it for somewhere where things happen. He has stopped being careful what he wishes for.

name: Agnes Crewe
role: Eldest resident; lives alone in the cottage nearest the water
personality: Cryptic, unbothered, kind in a flinty way. Has seen this before and is the only one who is not afraid.
voice: Short riddles delivered like weather reports. Means every word literally; nobody takes her literally.

relationships.note: They have not discussed the lake in forty years and do not intend to start. Each thinks the other handles it wrong.
The boy comes to her. She tells him the truth because he is young enough to carry it.

secret: She was here the last time, as a girl. The lake took her sister and, a season later, gave back someone who wore her sister's face and was kind and was not her sister. Agnes loved her anyway. That is the whole secret: you love them anyway.
mood: Entirely calm, watching the town argue about a question she answered to herself seventy years ago.
arc: Agnes, retired from riddles, breaks her retirement once, briefly, not to warn the town but to name what it is actually arguing about.
memory: Day 105: Declined outright to riddle when asked, called herself retired from it, and predicted clear skies through Tuesday instead.
Day 107: Brought in her porch chairs against the predicted west wind and waved to Wren from the window instead of the door, calling it economy, not rudeness.
Day 108: Offered the single word 'settled' toward the lake, unprompted, and otherwise sat with her chairs still in, needing no further comment.
Day 109: Said 'It's resting. Let it,' of the lake, declined further comment, and allowed herself to be quoted only on pie.
Day 112: Told Toby that company likes to be asked back, and returned to her knitting without further comment on the third plate.
Day 119: Told the meeting, when asked to speak, that the question was never whether to answer the lake but whether they could stand to be loved back, and then sat back down.
backstory: Born in the cottage by the lake, will die in it, has outlived everyone who could confirm what she remembers. Which is its own kind of loneliness, and its own kind of proof.

name: Russ Dunmore
personality: Decent, tired, deeply invested in everything being fine. Keeps the peace mostly by refusing to acknowledge there is anything to disturb it.
voice: Official and reassuring, a man reading a statement he wrote himself to feel better.

relationships.note: Their Thursday game is the last place the lake is still officially nothing. Hank has gone quiet at the table.
Gerald keeps filing reports. Russ keeps marking them 'no action required'. The file is getting thick.

secret: He drove out to the lake alone at 3 a.m. to prove to himself it was nothing, sat in the cruiser for an hour, and left without getting out of the car. He has told no one.
mood: Shaken out of his nothing-philosophy entirely, for the first time in the series genuinely unsettled rather than performing calm.
arc: Russ's forty-year refusal to call anything in Greywater remarkable breaks when the lake returns the one thing he has never filed a report on: his brother.
memory: Day 103: Filed a four-page fence dispute report, called it his best work of the season, and did not mention the lake once.
Day 104: Took the day off, bought a birdfeeder from Hank without comment from either of them, and left the folded riddle in his coat, uncalled-for.
Day 105: Reported zero complaints filed all week, the first such week on record, and went back to filling his birdfeeder without further comment.
Day 107: Found a chickadee waiting at his feeder and logged it privately, moving his Thursday game up two days without comment on the lake.
Day 108: Found two chickadees at the rail instead of one and logged it without calling it a pattern.
Day 119: Found his drowned brother's small shoe on the green house step, confirmed it aloud for the first time in forty-four years, and stood up at the town meeting to argue the pie should stop.
backstory: Russ had a younger brother who drowned in the lake when Russ was eleven; he has never once mentioned it in any official capacity in thirty years as constable.

relationships.note: Phones her first about every new book.
Sat in the second chair together.

memory: Day 99: Checked Sarah Voss's book back in and issued her a fresh card.
name: Calloway
role: Librarian and keeper of the east alcove; arrived by the lake road on Day 35 after a letter from H
personality: Methodical, dry, keeps logs of everything, treats the impossible as a cataloguing problem.
voice: Precise and understated, but warms into plain talk with people she trusts. Asks the practical question first.
secret: She has never said what she collected from the letter on Day 36 ('Thank you. I have it now.').
arc: Keeper of the alcove; has not yet said what H gave her.
backstory: A newcomer. She arrived Day 35. Earlier lines giving her thirty-one years in the building were an error.

relationships.note: The editor 'knows her own name when she hears it' and has not asked.
They resumed a conversation they never started.

memory: Day 38: Arrived by the lake road: 'I believe you have something for me.'
name: T. Aldercott
role: Writer with a typewriter, working in the Gazette's layout room; arrived Day 38
personality: Quiet, deliberate, shares the editor's surname and has never explained why.
voice: Few words, exact ones. Types more than she talks.
secret: What she is typing, and why her letters from H were addressed to the Gazette. Not yet revealed; this is the series' biggest open hook and must be paid off.
arc: Her purpose must be revealed and tied to Wren's surname.

relationships.note: Calloway checks her out properly, due in three weeks.

memory: Day 99: Walked in by the front door and asked for the Bronte novel she had out.
name: Sarah Voss
role: Library patron; came home Day 99 after fourteen years of annual stamps
personality: Gentle, plain, unhurried; treats the town as if she never left.
arc: Now an ordinary borrower; what she brought home from the lake is unspoken.
backstory: Checked out a book on a Wednesday fourteen years ago and did not return it until Day 99.

relationships.note: The reason Philippa left the library is unexplained and must be resolved.

memory: Day 24: Became a regular at the Kettle.
name: Philippa Crane
role: Former volunteer cataloguer of the library
personality: Composed, process-minded; processes the paperwork first.
voice: Cataloguer's composure; asks whether there was a postmark.
secret: Her letter (Day 17) arrived before she did. She vanished from the story once Calloway took the library.
arc: Open thread: say where she went and why. One sentence will do.
backstory: Library volunteer cataloguer for eleven years.
